blocks.text: URDA, Spain —A high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed 68 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, authorities said, in one of Europe’s deadliest such disasters this century. The second such accident to strike Spain this year will raise fresh questions about the country’s rail safety, with the transport minister speaking of an “error” and “inexplicable circumstances” that led to the crash. AFP reporters on the scene in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha saw one train embedded into another and some carriages lying on their side at the bottom of an embankment strewn with debris.
